rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall be responsible for the overall performance of the contract and provide all necessary resources to
meet contract requirements.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall be responsible for overall contract performance and provide all necessary resources to meet requirements.

rows.verbatim: All work completed under this contract shall comply with contract requirements.
rows.normalized: All work completed under the contract shall comply with contract requirements.

rows.verbatim:
All
deliverables under this contract shall not be marked proprietary or confidential or with any other markings limiting
the Government’s use, unless otherwise specified by the Government.
rows.normalized: Deliverables shall not be marked proprietary or confidential unless otherwise specified by the Government.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide services globally without exception.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide services globally without exception.

rows.verbatim:
In the event that the Contractor cannot provide a
medevac in specific parts of the world, then the Contractor shall provide sufficient rationale to the NASA COR why
it cannot and provide an alternate solution at no additional cost beyond the prepaid amount.
rows.normalized: If the Contractor cannot provide medevac in specific parts of the world, it shall provide rationale to the NASA COR and an alternate solution at no additional cost.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall be responsible for all medevac and medical travel service costs.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall be responsible for all medevac and medical travel service costs.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall ensure that any of the contractor’s owned, leased, or chartered aircraft used in the performance
of this contract comply with all applicable local and long‑distance aircraft and pilot requirements, including those
applicable to both prime contractors and subcontractors.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure owned, leased, or chartered aircraft comply with all applicable local and long-distance aircraft and pilot requirements, including for subcontractors.

rows.verbatim:
Aircraft used for NASA traveler transportation shall be
certificated, operated, and maintained in accordance with the requirements of 14 CFR:
a. Part 21—Certification Procedures for Products and Parts
b. Part 25—Airworthiness Standards: Transport Category Airplanes Part 29—Airworthiness Standards:
Transport Category Rotorcraft Part 39—Airworthiness Directives
c. Part 43—Maintenance, Preventative Maintenance, Rebuilding, and Alteration Part 61—Certification: Pilots,
Flight Instructors, and Ground Instructors
d. Part 65—Certification: Airmen Other Than Flight Crewmembers Part 91—General Operating and Flight Rules
e. Part 135—Operating Requirements: Commuter and On-Demand Operations
rows.normalized: Aircraft used for NASA traveler transportation shall be certificated, operated, and maintained per 14 CFR Parts 21, 25/29/39, 43/61, 65/91, and 135; 5 required parts in total.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall have a documented Safety Management System (SMS) in accordance with International Civil
Aviation Organization (ICAO), Federal, and industry standards. Requirements include the following:
a. A structured means of safety risk management decision making.
b. A means of demonstrating safety management capability before system failures occur.
c. Increased confidence in risk controls through structured safety assurance processes.
d. An effective interface for knowledge sharing.
e. A safety promotion framework to support a sound safety culture.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall have a documented Safety Management System meeting ICAO/Federal/industry standards; 5 SMS requirements listed.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall indemnify the Government for any occurrence, action, or claim that might trigger the
Government's liability; unless the Government is found to be liable.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall indemnify the Government for occurrences/claims triggering Government liability, unless the Government is found liable.

rows.verbatim:
The rights and obligations of the parties under
this clause shall survive the termination, expiration, or completion of this contract.
rows.normalized: The rights and obligations of the parties under this clause shall survive termination, expiration, or completion of the contract.

Contractor shall provide medical travel services worldwide including 14 listed services (transportation, medical coordination, pharmacy, monitoring, referrals, advocacy, case management, translation, hospital coordination, GOP services, repatriation, etc.).

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall transport the injured or ill traveler to nearest appropriate medical facility that practices U.S.
standards of medical care.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall transport injured/ill travelers to nearest facility practicing U.S. standards of medical care.

rows.verbatim:
a. In the event that the medical facility does not meet the U.S. standards of medical care, the Contractor shall
provide sufficient rationale to the NASA/JSC Chief Medical Officer and NASA Contracting Officer
Representative (COR) for using the proposed facility.
rows.normalized: If the medical facility does not meet U.S. standards, the Contractor shall provide rationale to the NASA/JSC Chief Medical Officer and COR for using it.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall co-develop with NASA the notification process for timely communication, integration and
operational protocols with NASA physicians, and dissemination of confidential medical reports.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall co-develop with NASA the notification process for communication, integration/operational protocols, and dissemination of confidential medical reports.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall obtain all necessary insurance information from the traveler, as required, and shall coordinate
the payment of personal medical expenses incurred by the traveler that are not arranged for or provided directly by
the Contractor.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall obtain necessary insurance information from the traveler and shall coordinate payment of personal medical expenses not arranged by the Contractor.

rows.verbatim:
Such coordination
shall be conducted exclusively between the Contractor, the traveler, and the
traveler’s insurer, without any involvement from the Government.
rows.normalized: Coordination of personal medical expense payment shall be conducted exclusively between Contractor, traveler, and traveler's insurer, without Government involvement.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide group membership as specified in Section B Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Group
Membership.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide group membership as specified in Section B FFP Group Membership.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide an “Air Ambulance Medical Evacuation” (medevac) service in response to a
worldwide medical emergency for NASA’s Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate (HSMD), Johnson Space
Center (JSC), or other travelers identified by NASA (referred to as ‘traveler(s)’ throughout) on a pre-paid basis
regardless of traveler’s home location or country of origin.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide Air Ambulance Medical Evacuation service worldwide for identified NASA travelers on a pre-paid basis.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide transportation for three accompanying travelers specified by NASA on the same transport as the injured/ill individual requiring a medevac.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide transport for three NASA-specified accompanying travelers on the same medevac transport.

rows.verbatim: In the event that the same transport cannot accommodate all three accompanying travelers, at least one accompanying traveler specified by NASA shall be accommodated on the same transport.
rows.normalized: If the transport cannot accommodate all three travelers, contractor must accommodate at least one NASA-specified traveler on the same transport.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide sufficient rationale to the NASA Contracting Officer Representative (COR) why it cannot transport all accompanying travelers and provide alternate transportation for the remaining accompanying travelers within 24 hours to the same location as the injured or ill traveler.
rows.normalized: Contractor must justify inability to transport all accompanying travelers to the COR and provide alternate transportation for remaining travelers within 24 hours.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor provided services shall meet the Commission on Accreditation Medical Transport Services (CAMTS), National Accreditation Alliance of Medical Transport Applications (NAAMTA) Global, and European Aero-Medical Institute (EURAMI) accreditation standards or equivalent for personnel and assets.
rows.normalized: Contractor's services must meet CAMTS, NAAMTA Global, and EURAMI accreditation standards or equivalent for personnel and assets.

rows.verbatim: Active credentials must be maintained according to the standard renewal timelines dictated by the respective accrediting body.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain active credentials per accrediting body renewal timelines.

rows.verbatim: Any deviations must be reported to the JSC Chief Medical Officer and Contracting Officer Representative (COR), and approved by NASA prior to implementation, unless otherwise specified by the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report any deviations to the JSC Chief Medical Officer and COR and obtain NASA approval before implementation, unless the CO specifies otherwise.

rows.verbatim: The decision to perform a medevac shall be made jointly (50/50) by NASA and the Contractor, who will apply U.S. standards of medical care.
rows.normalized: Decision to perform a medevac is made jointly by NASA and Contractor, applying U.S. medical care standards.

rows.verbatim: This independent third party will be mutually agreed upon within 30 calendar days of contract award.
rows.normalized: NASA and Contractor must mutually agree on an independent third party within 30 calendar days of contract award.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide a medical evacuation using a Portable Medical Isolation Unit (e.g. infectious disease) upon request by NASA.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide medevac using a Portable Medical Isolation Unit upon NASA's request.

rows.verbatim: If a medical event occurs, all costs for evacuation and additional medical travel services shall be the responsibility of the Contractor and no additional cost beyond the prepaid provided group membership as specified in Section B Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Group Membership amount will be incurred by NASA or its travelers.
rows.normalized: If a medical event occurs, contractor is responsible for all evacuation and additional medical travel costs beyond the prepaid group membership amount.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall conduct a program status meeting each contract year with NASA management and JSC’s Chief Medical Officer, with the first meeting happening within 90 calendar days of the start of the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must conduct an annual program status meeting with NASA management and JSC's Chief Medical Officer, first meeting within 90 days of contract start.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall participate in NASA Contingency Tabletop simulations of evacuation events to validate communication and operations plans and decision-making procedures (estimate twice per year).
rows.normalized: Contractor must participate in NASA Contingency Tabletop simulations (approx. twice per year).

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide, within 60 calendar days of contract start and update annually for currency by Oct 1st, a Medical Facility Support Plan for each of the Russia and Kazakhstan medical facilities identified by NASA which contains the following: a. Points of Contact (primary, alternate, and emergency) and communication protocols, including language/translation support and expected response times. b. Medical Capabilities and Transport Capabilities, including bed‑to‑bed transport feasibility, equipment availability, access to specialized care, and any seasonal or regional constraints that may affect operations.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide, within 60 days of contract start (updated annually by Oct 1), a Medical Facility Support Plan for Russia/Kazakhstan facilities containing listed elements; 8 required contents in total (items a-h, continued across page break).

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall establish and provide, within 60 calendar days of contract start and maintain for the duration of the contract, the GOP advance service agreements with the specific medical facilities that NASA identifies as critical medical facilities in Russia and Kazakhstan.
rows.normalized: Contractor must establish, provide within 60 days of contract start, and maintain GOP advance service agreements with NASA-identified critical medical facilities in Russia and Kazakhstan.

rows.verbatim: If the Contractor cannot establish a GOP advance service agreement at one of NASA’s identified medical facilities in Russia/Kazakhstan by the end of that 60-day period, then the Contractor shall notify the NASA COR and provide an alternate course of action to meet the intent of the GOP advance service agreement.
rows.normalized: If contractor cannot establish a GOP agreement within 60 days, it must notify the NASA COR and propose an alternate course of action.

rows.verbatim: Annually by December 15th, the Contractor shall provide a written summary report on the status of GOP advance service agreements for the NASA identified hospitals.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide an annual written summary report on GOP advance service agreement status by December 15.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall establish and provide, within 60 calendar days of contract start and updated annually for currency by Oct 1st, a written medevac plan of action/response for each location that NASA frequently visits to include Moscow, Russia; Baikonur, Kazakhstan; Karaganda, Kazakhstan; Nordwijk, Netherlands; Montreal, Canada; Tsukuba, Japan; and Tanegashima, Japan. The plan shall include at a minimum: a. Specific points of contact the Contractor will utilize to access restricted airports or facilities; b. Unique country and local specific requirements for medevac services and plans on how to address each; c. Specific facilities, capabilities, and transport services in country the Contractor will utilize for bed-to-bed medical transport including any operational limitations or risk factors; d. Transport and Access Considerations, including typical timelines and constraints for access to airports, border crossings, restricted areas, or local authorities. e. Regional Risk Assessment, summarizing relevant geopolitical, infrastructure, transportation, or environmental risks, along with proposed mitigation strategies. f. Whether selected medical providers accept U.S Government employee medical insurance plans; g. List of data and documentation the Contractor requires NASA to provide to support medevac. h. Verification and Validation Procedures, describing how the Contractor annually confirms the accuracy of facility information, capabilities, and points of contact data.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide, within 60 days of contract start (updated annually by Oct 1), a written medevac plan of action for each frequently-visited NASA location, including 8 listed elements (points of contact, requirements, facilities/capabilities, transport/access, risk assessment, insurance acceptance, data needs, verification procedures).

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide, within 10 calendar days of contract start, a secure electronic registration capability that: a. Provides travelers with a description of the scope of Contractor’s services in accordance with this SOW. b. Educates travelers on specific instructions to follow should a medical incident or emergency occur and traveler’s responsibilities in accordance with this SOW. c. Captures critical information from travelers that expedites medical assistance and evacuation when necessary. d. Meets industry standards for data protection, accessibility, storage, and retention requirements of private medical and personal information (e.g. Personally Identifiable Information, Health Insurance, etc.).
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide, within 10 days of contract start, a secure electronic registration capability meeting 4 listed functional requirements (scope description, traveler education, data capture, data protection standards).

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide a weekly report on current and historical NASA traveler enrollment and critical traveler information.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a weekly report on NASA traveler enrollment and critical traveler information.

rows.verbatim: Travelers will not be required to be pre-enrolled or registered in a Contractor’s system in order for the Contractor to provide services covered under this contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor may not require travelers to pre-enroll or register in its system as a condition of providing covered services.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide, by Sept 30th annually, a summary report of all medical incidents by date and incidence level (Levels 1-4), medical evacuations, reservations and call-ups of medical transport via air ambulance for Soyuz landings (if executed) supported by the Contractor during that year.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide, by Sept 30 annually, a summary report of medical incidents, evacuations, and Soyuz-landing air ambulance reservations/call-ups for that year.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide, within 60 calendar days after contract award, wallet sized cards to the NASA COR for every NASA traveler with information including an international call number for support for medical support and emergencies.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide wallet-sized cards to the NASA COR for every NASA traveler, within 60 days after contract award, including an international support call number.

rows.verbatim: Approximately 1,200 cards are required annually for NASA travelers.
rows.normalized: Contractor must produce approximately 1,200 wallet cards annually for NASA travelers.

rows.verbatim: The cards shall be updated for currency and provided annually thereafter to the NASA COR by Oct 1st.
rows.normalized: Contractor must update and provide the cards annually to the NASA COR by Oct 1.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide a Reservation and Call-up/Execution service for medical transport via air ambulance for Soyuz crew landing event.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a Reservation and Call-up/Execution service for air ambulance medical transport for Soyuz crew landing events.

rows.verbatim: Within 36 hours of NASA reservation, the Contractor shall provide a Reservation Readiness Package consisting of a dedicated tail-number assignment, overflight and landing permits, diplomatic route clearances, aircraft medical and transport capabilities, and staffing plan.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a Reservation Readiness Package within 36 hours of NASA's reservation, including tail-number assignment, permits, clearances, capabilities, and staffing plan.

rows.verbatim: NASA will provide call-up/execute notification to the Contractor no later than 36 hours prior to the Soyuz landing event.
rows.normalized: NASA will notify the Contractor of call-up/execution no later than 36 hours before Soyuz landing, establishing the Contractor's response trigger.

rows.verbatim: The crew member and the associated NASA flight surgeon shall be transported to Houston, Texas.
rows.normalized: The crew member and NASA flight surgeon must be transported to Houston, Texas (by the Contractor).

rows.verbatim: Within 3 hours of the NASA call-up, the Contractor shall activate the asset and personnel and provide an Operational Deployment Package consisting of a copy of the officially filed International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) flight plan, crew-rest compliance, real-time satellite tracking link, confirmation of NASA passengers on flight manifest, finalized staffing plan, and communications matrix.
rows.normalized: Contractor must activate asset/personnel and provide an Operational Deployment Package within 3 hours of NASA's call-up, including flight plan, crew-rest compliance, tracking link, manifest confirmation, staffing plan, and communications matrix.

rows.verbatim: Once a NASA flight surgeon determines the traveler is fit-to-fly, there is no requirement for an observation or stabilization period at a local medical facility prior to medical transport via air ambulance.
rows.normalized: Once a NASA flight surgeon determines fit-to-fly, contractor is not required to provide an observation/stabilization period before medical transport.

rows.verbatim: If a reservation or call-up for medical transport via air ambulance occurs, all costs for the reservation and medical transport via air ambulance shall be the responsibility of the Contractor and no additional cost beyond the prepaid reservation fee and call-up fee as specified in Section B Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Group Membership amount will be incurred by NASA or its travelers.
rows.normalized: If a reservation or call-up occurs, contractor is responsible for all associated costs beyond the prepaid reservation/call-up fees.

rows.verbatim: The Offeror must submit a statement of verification that, as of the date of its offer, its representations and certifications posted electronically in www.SAM.gov for the provisions listed in FAR 52.204-19 - Incorporation by Reference of Representations and Certifications Section I above, are current, accurate, and complete.
rows.normalized: The Offeror must submit a statement verifying its SAM.gov representations and certifications are current, accurate, and complete.

rows.verbatim: The Offeror shall prepare their proposal in accordance with the instructions in this solicitation.
rows.normalized: The Offeror shall prepare its proposal per the solicitation's instructions.

rows.verbatim: Information contained in the Offeror’s proposal must be in sufficient detail to allow adequate assessment of for Technical Capability and Price.
rows.normalized: The Offeror's proposal must contain sufficient detail to allow assessment of Technical Capability and Price.

rows.verbatim: The Offerors’ proposal must contain the absolute best offer as the Government has the right to award without discussions.
rows.normalized: The Offeror's proposal must contain its absolute best offer.

rows.verbatim: All proposal data shall be provided in Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Word or PDF formats only.
rows.normalized: The Offeror shall provide all proposal data only in Excel, Word, or PDF format.

rows.verbatim:
The proposal shall include the following:
1. Technical Capability
a. Questions/Responses as annotated below.
b. Scenarios as annotated below.
2. Pricing - Must include “Offeror Fill-In” (OFI) blocks with table as annotated in Section B above.
3. Representations and Certifications – Statement of verification as annotated in Section K above.
rows.normalized: The proposal shall include Technical Capability (Questions/Responses, Scenarios), Pricing (OFI blocks), and Representations and Certifications.

rows.verbatim: Please only submit an electronic copy of your proposal.
rows.normalized: The Offeror shall submit only an electronic copy of the proposal.

rows.verbatim: DO NOT compress any electronic files.
rows.normalized: The Offeror shall not compress any electronic files.

rows.verbatim: DO NOT password protect any portion of your electronic submission.
rows.normalized: The Offeror shall not password protect any part of the electronic submission.

rows.verbatim: The Government intends to make a single award for all items on an "all or none" basis; therefore, Offerors must provide a proposal that responds to all items below.
rows.normalized: Offerors must provide a proposal responding to all items, as award will be all-or-none.

rows.verbatim: Partial quotes will not be considered responsible to this solicitation and therefore not accepted.
rows.normalized: Partial quotes will not be accepted or considered responsive.

rows.verbatim: The Offeror shall state in their offer their size status for this procurement.
rows.normalized: The Offeror shall state its small business size status in its offer.

rows.verbatim: Offerors must provide responses to these areas in sufficient detail to demonstrate responsiveness to the solicitation.
rows.normalized: Offerors must provide responses in sufficient detail to demonstrate responsiveness.

rows.verbatim: Responses shall be submitted in a Microsoft Word document in Times New Roman, size 12 font.
rows.normalized: Responses shall be submitted as a Word document in Times New Roman, size 12 font.

rows.verbatim: a. Describe the offeror’s approach, teaming arrangements, resources, processes and procedures to provide worldwide medical evacuation and medical travel services capabilities per the requirements of the Statement of Work (SOW).
rows.normalized: The Offeror shall describe its approach, teaming arrangements, resources, processes, and procedures for worldwide medical evacuation/travel services per the SOW.

rows.verbatim:
The Offeror shall explain its capabilities and expected operational timelines/durations with medical
extractions for potential life or death circumstances with a point of origin in a non-western country similar in size, scope,
and complexity to the requirements in the SOW and scenarios.
rows.normalized: The Offeror shall explain its capabilities/timelines for medical extractions from non-western countries for life-or-death circumstances.

rows.verbatim:
The Offeror shall explain how it flows down the contract
terms and conditions to its subcontractors and teaming partners.
rows.normalized: The Offeror shall explain how it flows down contract terms and conditions to subcontractors/teaming partners.

rows.verbatim:
The Offeror shall explain its capabilities and expected
operational timelines/durations with medical transport via air ambulance reservation and call up for NASA Astronauts
participating in Soyuz landings and return to the US.
rows.normalized: The Offeror shall explain its capabilities/timelines for air ambulance reservation and call-up for Soyuz landing astronauts.

rows.verbatim:
The Offeror shall provide a compliance matrix (cross-walk table)
explicitly mapping each element of the Statement of Work (SOW) to the specific section and page number where it is
addressed in the Technical Capability Proposal.

rows.verbatim:
b. Describe the air and ground transportation assets (type/design/age/capabilities/locations) your company uses to provide
worldwide medical evacuations per the requirements of the Statement of Work (SOW). What types of certifications do
these assets hold and where are they certificated (US, other country)? Does the Offeror maintain a fleet of its own fixed
wing and rotary aircraft required for medical transport or does it subcontract aircraft from other companies (If other
companies, which ones)? To what standards are the aircraft maintained (FAA, foreign equivalent, other) and is the
maintenance provider FAA Part 145 (or equivalent) certified? Does the aircraft provider have a Safety Management
System (SMS) in place (For example International Standard for Business Aircraft Operations (IS-BAO))?
rows.normalized: The Offeror shall describe its air/ground transportation assets and answer related certification, maintenance, and SMS questions.

rows.verbatim:
c. With regard to pilots used by Offeror for local and long-distance transport, does the Offeror maintain their own pilot
cadre or does it subcontract pilots from other companies (If other companies, which ones)? Where, how, and to what
standards are the pilots certified (For example FAA Commercial/Airline Transport Pilot (ATP), international equivalent)?
To which medical standards are the pilots held (i.e. FAA, Class I/II, other)? What are the minimum experience levels of
the pilots (flight time, international operations, IFR operations, etc./i.e. minimum 1500 hours turbine/multi-engine etc.)?
What recurrent training and minimum proficiency requirements are mandated for the pilots (i.e. FAA Part 121 or Part 135
recurring training requirements)? Does the source of the pilot cadre have a Safety Management System (SMS) in place
(for example IS-BAO)?

2. Advanced medication management in flight (anti-seizure meds, IV meds, etc.)
3. Advanced Cardiac Life Support
4. Medical Escort Services
5. Medevac Using Portable Medical Isolation Unit (e.g. infectious disease medevac)
rows.normalized: The Offeror shall provide evidence of capability to provide 5 listed advanced medical services.

applied to your subcontractors and teaming partners?
